text:
The symptoms trace to the cascode gate bias of M2. M10's source sits on Rn, and Rn's value is far too large. With M10 carrying about 2.02 µA, Rn = 265.8 kΩ drops about 0.53 V, so nd ≈ 0.53 V. M10 is diode-connected with Vgs ≈ 0.764 V, which puts nc ≈ 1.29 V. That matches the reported M2 Vgs of 1.27 V.

That gate voltage is too high for M2 to stay in saturation. M2 turns into a closed switch, pulls vout down to about 0.03 V, and drags M1 into triode (Vds = 0.031 V). The gain, GBW, and output-DC failures all follow from that. The M1 and M2 triode flags are symptoms of this bias error, not independent faults. Rn is the only element that is both out of range for this bias network and explains the nc voltage. The sensitivity table does not include Rn, so this ranking rests on the operating-point arithmetic rather than on the sensitivity data.
